description: Changes an account's own attributes — its name, its type (`tag` — the same words as the app's Account Type), its `notes`, the person it belongs to (`member`), its balance with the day it was true, and the account it is linked to (`linked_to`) — by id or the exact name as the memory holds it — a miss answers with the real names. `notes` holds what is particular about the account, one detail per line, such as a card's printed name as "Card name: Platinum Reserve"; numbers are refused. card_name and details are longbook's own, and a set sending a non-empty one is refused. Everything not named stays as it was; an explicit null clears. A balance carries its date; left out, the day of the write is used. A linked account is one level only: a card to the bank account that pays it, never a chain. `member` and `linked_to` name rows the memory already holds. Renaming onto a name another account wears is refused rather than merged. Writes are schema-validated and provenance-stamped, and land in the app's Proposals screen where the owner keeps or undoes the whole batch. Card numbers, CVVs and credentials are refused by the validator, which names the row. `source` ("documents/hdfc-2026.pdf", "gmail:18c2…") records where a row came from in the diff.

guide_key.description: The guide_key read_guide returned with the prompt or chapter this write follows.

linked_to.description: The account this one is linked to — a card to the bank account that pays it — by name or id. One level only. Null clears.

member.description: The person the account belongs to, by name or id. Null or "" clears.

notes.description: What is particular about the account, one detail per line, each "Label: value" — on a card, "Card name: Platinum Reserve", the product printed on it; its number is refused. Rewritten as the account now stands. Null or "" clears.

parent.description: An older name for linked_to, still accepted.

parent_account.description: An older name for linked_to, still accepted.
